channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Iran accuses US of 'reckless military adventure'
item.description: Iran accused the US of a reckless military adventure. Abbas Araghchi said the US attacks when a diplomatic solution is near. Abbas Araghchi says the US attacks each time there is a diplomatic solution on the table.

item.title: U.S., Iran could resume talks in Islamabad next week, says report
item.description: The US disabled two Iranian tankers to enforce a port blockade. Iranian officials accused the US of violating the ceasefire. A U. S. fighter jet disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers to enforce a port blockade, Iranian officials accused the United States of violating the ceasefire with the tanker strikes and hampering diplomatic efforts to end the conflict.

item.title: China trade beats forecasts in April despite Middle East war
item.description: China's April trade beat forecasts despite the Middle East war. Its economy has weathered disruptions so far. While the US-Israel war on Iran has produced new risks for China's economy, its trade has so far appeared to be weathering the disruptions.

item.title: India, IOM discuss expanding, diversifying regular migration pathways
item.description: India discussed expanding regular migration pathways with the IOM. Talks focused on implementation of GCM activities in India. "Discussions focussed on expanding and diversifying regular migration pathways and on India’s proactive approach to the implementation of GCM and IOM activities in India," Kirti Vardhan Singh said.

item.title: Tehran could withstand blockade for four months, CIA report shows, as fighting flares
item.description: A CIA report shows Tehran could withstand a blockade for four months. Fighting has flared in the Strait of Hormuz. Recent days have seen the biggest ‌flare-ups in fighting in and around the Strait of Hormuz since a ceasefire began a month ago, and the United Arab Emirates came under renewed attack on Friday (May 8, 2026).

item.title: Argentina's Hot Spot For Antarctic Cruises Insists It Didn't Cause Outbreak
item.description: Argentina's Tierra del Fuego province denied causing a hantavirus outbreak. Officials want investigations into other provinces visited by passengers. Officials in Argentina's Tierra del Fuego province are challenging the idea that the ongoing deadly hantavirus outbreak may have emerged there, pushing instead for investigations into the other Argentine provinces that passengers visited before board.

item.title: U.S. strikes two Iranian-flagged vessels as tensions continue amid ceasefire
item.description: The US struck two Iranian-flagged vessels amid ongoing tensions. The incident occurred as a ceasefire was in place. The US action was reported by The Washington Post. U. S. strikes two Iranian-flagged vessels as tensions continue amid ceasefire The Washington Post.

item.title: Cricket gives special dimension to India-Trinidad and Tobago ties: Jaishankar
item.description: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar visited Trinidad and Tobago, highlighting cricket's role in India-Trinidad and Tobago ties. He arrived in Port of Spain from Paramaribo on May 8. Jaishankar arrived in Port of Spain from Paramaribo on May 8, 2026 on the concluding leg of his three-nation tour of Jamaica, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago.

item.title: Trump Says His Administration Is "Closely Monitoring" Cases
item.description: The WHO notified 12 countries, including the UK and US, about potential exposure to a virus after passengers disembarked at Saint Helena. The countries were informed to monitor for cases.

item.title: Day 70 of Middle East conflict . US hopes for ‘serious offer’ from Iran
item.description: Trump expects Iran's response to a proposal to end the war despite an exchange of fire. Live updates: Trump expects Iran’s response soon on proposal to end war, despite exchange of fire CNN.

item.title: North Korea to deploy new artillery along border with South
item.description: North Korea will deploy a new 155-millimetre self-propelled gun-howitzer along its border with South Korea. The move could put Seoul within striking range. Deployment of the "new-type 155-millimetre self-propelled gun-howitzer" would potentially place Seoul within striking range.

item.title: Trump says Russia and Ukraine have agreed to his request for a 3-day ceasefire
item.description: US President Trump said Russia and Ukraine agreed to a three-day ceasefire. Presidents Zelenskyy and Putin's adviser Ushakov confirmed the deal, which includes a prisoner exchange. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Yuri Ushakov, President Vladimir Putin's foreign affairs adviser, both confirmed the agreement for a three-day ceasefire and an exchange of prisoners.

item.title: U.K. PM Starmer says he won’t step down after Labour’s losses
item.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer refused to step down after Labour's losses, citing a need to avoid plunging the country into chaos. He acknowledged the results were "really tough" but vowed to continue leading the party.

item.title: Peter Magyar Prepares to Take Over as Hungary’s Leader From Viktor Orban
item.description: Peter Magyar is set to take over as Hungary's leader from Viktor Orban after winning a landslide election. He faces the challenge of dismantling Orban's self-described "illiberal democracy" and restoring democratic institutions.

item.title: Punch, the Lonely Monkey Who Drew Crowds to a Small Japan Zoo, Is Growing Up. He’s Still a Star.
item.description: A 9-month-old macaque monkey named Punch continues to draw tens of thousands of visitors to a small Japanese zoo. Despite the attention, Punch remains unfazed and ignores the crowds. The macaque, now 9 months old, has been attracting tens of thousands of visitors to a small Japanese zoo.

item.title: A Less Muscular Victory Day Parade Shows Putin’s Growing Vulnerability
item.description: Russia's Victory Day parade was scaled back due to security concerns, showcasing Putin's growing vulnerability. The reduced event adds to a sense that Moscow and other cities are no longer insulated from the war.

item.title: How China’s Leader Lost Faith in His Generals
item.description: Chinese leader Xi Jinping's trust in his generals has waned despite building a military to rival the US. Over 13 years, Xi handpicked top brass but grew increasingly uneasy with their loyalty and competence.

item.title: In Hungary, Viktor Orban Loyalists Jump Ship
item.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban's loyalists are defecting in large numbers, with many jumping ship before the incoming prime minister, Peter Magyar, can push out what he calls "puppets of the old regime." Magyar has promised to bring change.

item.title: Trump expects Iran’s response on peace deal offer 'as soon as tonight'
item.description: US President Trump expects Iran's response to a peace deal offer by tonight. The offer was made in an attempt to ease tensions between the two countries. Trump expects Iran’s response on peace deal offer 'as soon as tonight' USA Today.

item.title: Muted U.S. Response to Iranian Attacks Deepens Gulf Fears About Cease-Fire
item.description: The US has responded mildly to recent Iranian attacks, deepening fears in the Gulf region that a cease-fire may not hold. The muted response has raised concerns about the effectiveness of the agreement.
